FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Food Microbiology Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division 
Council. 


Unless the ingredients used in media for microbiological work are of uniform quality, the results obtained might 
be erroneous and might be unreliable. Since the media used in different laboratories often differ greatly in their 
quality, the results of microbiological work at different laboratories cannot be compared. Therefore, with a view 
to unifying the practices of different laboratories dealing with microbiology and providing guidance to the 
indigenous manufacturers regarding the quality, it was decided to bring out a series of Indian Standard 
specifications for ingredients commonly used in media for microbiological work. For specific purposes, any 
additional requirements shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 


Agar is prepared from a variety of sea-weeds. In microbiological work, it is used as a solidifying agent for media. 
There is considerable variation in the quality of agar and depends upon the source of raw material, method of 
collection and subsequent manufacture. It is usually commercially available in bundles consisting of their 
membranous strips or in cut, flaked, granulated, or powdered forms. 


This standard was first published in 1973. The first revision of the standard has been brought out to incorporate 
following modifications keeping in view the technological advancements in this area along with the editorial 
changes to align it in the latest style and format of Indian Standard: 


a) Requirement of colour at 3.1 has been changed from ‘white to pale yellow’ to ‘cream coloured’; 

b) Requirement of ‘clarity’ has been shifted into Table 1 assigning specific value and method of test to it; 

c) Method of test for the requirement of ‘gelatin’ has been modified; 

d) Method of test for the requirement of ‘insoluble matter’ has been rewritten in the simplified form for better 
clarity; and 

e) Anew requirement of ‘Starch’ has been added along with its method of test as starch is being used as an 
adulterant in the product, which makes the agar solution or gel opalescent and starch being easy source of 
carbon make the agar more prone to contamination by fungi and bacteria. 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex E. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 6850 : 2023 


Indian Standard 
AGAR, MICROBIOLOGICAL GRADE — SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and 
methods of test for agar, microbiological grade. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed below contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of these standards listed below: 


IS No. Title 


IS 1070: 1992 Reagent grade water — 
Specification (third revision) 


IS 6854: 1973 Methods of sampling and test for 
ingredients used in media for 
microbiological work 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Agar, microbiological grade shall be homogenous 
and cream coloured. 


3.2 Gelling Temperature 


On cooling the material, a concentration of not more 
than 2 percent shall solidify to form a stable gel at 
not more than 40 °C. This gel shall not liquefy below 
85 °C. 


NOTE — The gel should be formed in a test tube with a 
thermometer immersed in it before setting the gel. The gel 
should be just sufficient to dip the mercury bulb. Heating 
should be indirect in a water bath heated on a hot plate with 
slow heat. 


3.2.1 When autoclaved at 121 °C for 30 min and then 
cooled, the material shall form stable gel. 


3.2.2 After autoclaving twice at 121 °C for 30 min, 
a 2 percent aqueous solution of agar shall maintain a 
stable gel on cooling. 


3.3 The agar shall form a clear solution just below 
100 °C when heated with excess water. It shall have 
clarity when dissolved in media and shall be 
reasonably free from any suspended material. It shall 
comply to the requirement given at Table 1, 
SI No. (i). 


3.4 One and a half percent aqueous solution should 
have a pH between 6 and 8. 


3.5 The material shall not inhibit the growth of 
microorganisms when it is incorporated in a 
medium. This may be tested in the following 
manner: 


Prepare nutrient agar medium using the agar under 
test. Inoculate three plates of the medium with a 
strain of Escherichia coli. Incubate at 37 °C for 
24 h. There shall be no inhibition of growth of the 
microorganism and the growth shall exhibit the 
normal characteristics of the strain. 


3.6 The medium prepared with | percent to 2 percent 
of agar shall be firm when tested by streaking with a 
bacteriological loop. 


3.7 It shall also conform to the requirements given 
in Table 1. 


4 PACKING, STORAGE AND MARKING 
4.1 Packing 


The material shall be securely packed in well-filled 
wide mouth containers with tightly fitting lids. 


4.2 Storage 
The material shall be stored in a cool and dry place. 
4.3 Marking 


Each container shall be marked legibly to give the 
following information: 


a) Name of the material including the words 
‘Microbiological Grade’; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Minimum net quantity; and 

d) Batch or code number. 


4.3.1 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provision of 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and Rules and 
Regulations framed thereunder and the product(s) 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


IS 6850 : 2023 


5 SAMPLING 

The representative samples of the material shall be 
drawn according to the method prescribed in 
IS 6854. 

6 TESTS 


6.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods 
prescribed in 3 and in col (4) and (5) of Table 1. 


6.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
distilled water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in 
tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the experimental results.

(Clauses 3.3 and 3.7)

ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. (i)] 
DETERMINATION OF CLARITY 


A-1 REAGENTS 

A-1.1 Hydrazine Sulphate 

A-1.2 Hexamethylene Tetramine 

A-1.3 Standard Stock Standard (4 000 NTU) 


Prepare Solution A by adding 5g of Hydrazine 
sulphate in 400 ml of distilled water. Similarly, 
prepare Solution B by adding 50 g of Hexamethylene 
Tetramine in 400 ml of distilled water. Mix Solution 
A and B and make the volume up to 1 litre by adding 
distilled water. Allow the mixture to settle for 48 h at 
ambient temperature. This solution is usually stable 
for a period of 6 to 8 months. 


A-1.4 Working Standards 


Following working standards are prepared from 
stock standard: 


Volume of Stock Final Strength (conc.) 
Solution (ml) to Make of Formazin in Diluted 
up 1 Litre with Stock Solution (NTU) 
Distilled Water 


125.0 500 
25.5 100 
12.5 50 
20.0 of 500 NTU 10 
solution 
10.0 of 500 NTU 5 
solution 
20.0 of 50 NTU 1 


solution 


A-2 APPARATUS 
A-2.1 Turbidity Meter 
A-3 PROCEDURE 


Take 100 ml distilled water in a clean and dry flask. 
Weigh desired amount of agar powder under test and 
add it to the flask containing distilled water to form 
desired concentration (%) of solution in w/v. Mix the 
powder uniformly by swirling and record the pH. 
Autoclave the flask at 121 °C at 15 psi for 
15 minutes. After autoclaving, the flask is swirled to 
mix the solution uniformly and to avoid entrapment 
of air bubbles in case of viscous samples. The 
turbidity of the solution is measured using Turbidity 
Meter. 


IS 6850 : 2023 


ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. (v)] 
DETERMINATION OF GELATIN 


B-1 REAGENT 

B-1.1 Potassium Dichromate Solution, 0.2 M 
B-1.2 Hydrochloric Acid, 3N 

B-2 PROCEDURE 

B-2.1 Sample Solution 


Dissolve | g of sample in 100 ml of boiling water. 


Allow to cool to about 50 °C. 
B-2.2 Analysis 


To 5.0 ml of the sample solution, add 2 drops to 
3 drops of a mixture of 0.2 M potassium 
dichromate solution and 3 N HCL (4: 1). 


B-3 RESULT INTERPRETATION 


No yellow precipitate shall be formed. 


ANNEX C 
[Table 1, SI No. (vi)] 
DETERMINATION OF INSOLUBLE MATTER 


C-1 PROCEDURE 

C-1.1 Sample Dispersion 

Add sufficient water to 7.5 g of sample to make 
500 g, boil for 15 min, and readjust to the original 
500 g. 

C-1.2 Analysis 


To 100 g of the uniformly mixed sample dispersion, 
add hot water to make 200 ml. Heat almost to 


boiling, filter while hot through a tared filtering 
crucible. Rinse the container with several portions of 
hot water and pass these rinsings through the 
crucible. Dry the crucible and its contents at 105 °C 
to a constant weight. 


C-2 RESULT INTERPRETATION 
Not more than 15 mg (corresponding to 1 percent of 


the original sample weight) shall remain in the 
crucible. 


ANNEX D 
[Table 1, SI No. (vii)] 
DETERMINATION OF STARCH 


D-1 REAGENT 
D-1.1 Iodine Solution, 0.1 N 


Dissolve about 1.4 g of iodine in a solution of 3.6 g 
of potassium iodide in 100 ml of water. Add 3 drops 
of hydrochloric acid. Dilute with water to 1 000 ml. 


D-2 PROCEDURE 
D-2.1 Preparation of Sample solution 


Boil 0.1 g agar in 100 ml of water. 


D-2.2 Analysis 


Upon cooling up to 50 °C, the sample solution does 
not produce a blue color on addition of 
0.05 ml of 0.1 N iodine solution. 


ANNEX E 
(Foreword) 


IS 6850 : 2023

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
